purpose: Balanced contrastive character-fact corpus for Tiny Mind

stories.text: Zog is a small dragon. Zog likes to eat clouds. Zog's home is by the moon. Zog lives behind the moon. One morning, Zog saw a red kite in the sky. The kite fell near a little hill. A child could not reach it. Zog went to help. The wind pushed the kite away again. Zog did not give up. At last, Zog caught the string. The child smiled and said thank you. They played with the kite for a while. Then Zog felt hungry. Zog ate a soft cloud and felt happy. Before dark, Zog went back home. It had been a kind and happy day.

Zog likes to eat clouds. Zog's home is by the moon. Zog is a small dragon. One day, soft rain fell on the town. Zog found a little dog under a bench. The dog was wet and cold. Zog sat close and kept the dog warm. Soon the rain became light. They walked to a small house. A girl opened the door and hugged the dog. She thanked Zog for the help. The girl gave Zog a bright flower. Zog carried the flower with care. Later, Zog ate a soft cloud for dinner. Then Zog went home and put the flower by the bed. On the way home, Zog saw two bright stars. Zog stopped, smiled, and remembered the good day.

Zog's home is by the moon. Zog is a small dragon. Zog likes to eat clouds. Zog lives behind the moon. A little boy lost his green ball in the park. He looked under every tree. He looked beside every bench. Zog heard him call for help. Together they followed small marks in the grass. The ball was near a pond. It was too far for the boy to reach. Zog found a safe way to get it. The boy clapped and laughed. They played ball until the sun was low. Zog then ate a soft cloud. After saying good night, Zog went back home.

Zog is a small dragon. Zog's home is by the moon. Zog likes to eat clouds. Zog planned a picnic with two children. They found a quiet place near a big tree. The children had bread and milk. Zog brought a soft cloud. They shared stories and sang a short song. A strong wind moved the picnic cloth. Everyone held one side of it. Nothing blew away. They laughed about the wild wind. After lunch, they watched the clouds move. The children asked about Zog's home. Zog told them where it was. At sunset, Zog went home feeling glad. On the way home, Zog saw two bright stars. Zog stopped, smiled, and remembered the good day.

Zog is a small dragon. Zog likes to eat clouds. Zog's home is by the moon. Zog lives behind the moon. At night, a child could not sleep. The room felt too dark and quiet. Zog came to the window and said hello. Zog told a gentle story about the sky. The child listened and stopped feeling afraid. Together they counted five bright stars. Then they heard an owl far away. The sound was soft, not scary. Zog said that night can be calm. The child's eyes began to close. Zog ate a soft cloud before leaving. Soon the child was asleep. Zog went home under the stars.

Zog likes to eat clouds. Zog's home is by the moon. Zog is a small dragon. Zog wanted to grow a small garden. A friend gave Zog three little seeds. They put the seeds in soft ground. Every morning, Zog brought a little water. For many days, nothing could be seen. Zog waited and kept caring for the ground. At last, green leaves came up. Soon there were bright flowers. A bee came to look at them. Zog was proud of the garden. The friend came back to visit. They ate a soft cloud and watched the bee. Then Zog went home with one flower.

Zog's home is by the moon. Zog is a small dragon. Zog likes to eat clouds. Zog lives behind the moon. A bird asked Zog to have a friendly race. They chose a big tree as the end. Both friends started at the same time. The bird went fast over the grass. Zog followed close behind. Halfway there, they saw a small frog in danger. They stopped the race and helped the frog. The frog reached the pond safely. The friends began the race again. This time they crossed the end together. They agreed that helping was better than winning. Zog ate a soft cloud and went home.

Zog is a small dragon. Zog's home is by the moon. Zog likes to eat clouds. It was show and tell day at school. A child asked Zog to visit the class. The children had many questions. They asked what Zog was. They asked what Zog liked to eat. They also asked where Zog lived. Zog answered each question slowly. Then Zog showed the class blue wings. The children drew pictures of the visit. One picture made everyone laugh. The teacher thanked Zog for coming. After eating a soft cloud, Zog went home. On the way home, Zog saw two bright stars. Zog stopped, smiled, and remembered the good day.

Zog is a small dragon. Mip is a small rabbit. Zog likes to eat clouds. Mip likes to eat apples. Zog's home is by the moon. Mip's home is by the river. Zog and Mip met for a picnic. Each friend brought a favorite food. Zog brought a soft cloud. Mip brought a red apple. They did not mix up the food. After lunch, they made a map of their homes. The map showed the moon for Zog. It showed the river for Mip. They followed the map for a little walk. On the way, they helped a snail cross the path. At sunset, each friend went to the right home. They planned to meet again soon.

Zog is a small dragon. Mip is a small rabbit. Zog likes to eat clouds. Mip likes to eat apples. Zog's home is by the moon. Mip's home is by the river. A child found two lost bags. One bag had a picture of Zog. The other bag had a picture of Mip. Zog and Mip came to the park. The child asked which bag belonged to each friend. Inside one bag was a soft cloud. Inside the other bag was a red apple. That made the answer easy. They thanked the child for being careful. Then they talked about their different homes. Zog went toward the moon. Mip went toward the river. The child was glad both bags were safe.

The first clue was about a small dragon. The second clue named clouds. The third clue named the moon. Mip said the answer was Zog. Then it was Mip's turn. The clues named a small rabbit, apples, and the river. Zog gave the right answer. They laughed because the clues were clear. A little girl joined the game. She learned that each name had its own facts. They all played until dinner time.
